does: Wets a thick slice of firm cheese, coats it in flour and fries it in hot oil until a golden crust forms on both sides and the inside turns soft and molten, then serves it at once in the pan.

intro.what: A slice of firm cheese is floured and fried hot and fast until crusty outside and soft inside.
intro.why: The crust holds the soft cheese together. Too slow, and the cheese melts into the pan before the crust forms.

how: Cut the cheese into thick slices and dip each one in cold water.
Turn the wet slices in flour and shake off the excess.
Heat a little oil in a small heavy pan until it is very hot.
Fry the slices until a deep golden crust forms underneath, turn them once with a spatula, and fry the other side.
Serve at once, in the pan if you can, while the inside is soft.

cues.text: A loud sizzle the moment the cheese touches the oil.
A deep golden, blistered crust and soft cheese bulging at the sides.

mistakes.mistake: Oil that is not hot enough, so that the cheese melts and spreads before a crust forms.
mistakes.fix: Wait until the oil is very hot.

mistakes.mistake: Thin slices, which melt right through and lose their shape.
Leaving it to wait, so that the cheese turns rubbery.
mistakes.fix: Eat it as soon as it comes out of the pan.

quiz.question: Why must the oil be very hot?
choices: So that a crust forms before the cheese melts away.
quiz.because: The crust holds the cheese together.

quiz.question: Why dip the cheese in water first?
choices: So that the flour sticks in an even coat.
quiz.because: A wet surface holds a thin, even layer of flour.

variant_of.differs: The food is firm cheese, wetted and floured, fried very hot and fast only until a crust forms, and served at once, in the pan in which it was fried.
